suggestions.clause: Scope of the Agreement; Work Orders; Nature of Services; Transfer of Obligations
suggestions.reason: The current drafting uses "may include" followed by a broad catch-all for "other research and development services requested by Sponsor," which leaves the outer boundary of the Services undefined and exposes Quintiles, Inc. to scope-creep claims by Sponsor for work not contemplated or priced in any Work Order. Because the clause contains no express exclusion of services not set forth in an executed Work Order, Sponsor could assert that ad hoc requests fall within the Agreement's coverage even absent a signed Work Order, creating financial and operational risk for Quintiles, Inc. Anchoring scope exclusively to executed Work Orders and adding an express out-of-scope carve-out eliminates that exposure.
suggestions.original_text: Nature of Services. The services covered by this Agreement may include expert consultation, clinical trial services, statistical programming and analysis, clerical, project management, central laboratory services, preclinical services, pharmaceutical sciences services, and related data processing, data management and regulatory services, and other research and development services requested by Sponsor and agreed to by Quintiles as set forth in the relevant Work Order (collectively, the “Services”).
suggestions.suggested_fix: Nature of Services. The Services covered by this Agreement shall be limited to those services expressly set forth in the relevant Work Order, which may include expert consultation, clinical trial services, statistical programming and analysis, clerical, project management, central laboratory services, preclinical services, pharmaceutical sciences services, and related data processing, data management and regulatory services, and other research and development services requested by Sponsor and agreed to by Quintiles as set forth in the relevant Work Order (collectively, the "Services"). Any services not expressly described in an executed Work Order are outside the scope of this Agreement and Quintiles, Inc. shall have no obligation to perform them.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the clause contains no late-payment remedy — no interest, suspension right, or other consequence — leaving Quintiles, Inc. with no contractual leverage if Sponsor delays payment beyond the thirty (30) day period, which directly threatens the cash-neutrality objective the clause purports to protect. The clause also defers all fee-calculation methodology to each Work Order without requiring that Work Orders specify the basis of calculation (fixed-fee, time-and-materials, or otherwise), creating a risk that disputed Work Order terms could leave Quintiles unable to enforce its fee entitlement. Additionally, there is no mechanism to adjust fees if the scope of Services changes, exposing Quintiles to uncompensated scope creep between Work Order amendments.
suggestions.original_text: Payment of Fees and Expenses. Sponsor will pay Quintiles for fees, expenses and pass-through costs in accordance with the budget and payment schedule contained in each Work Order. Sponsor agrees that the budget and payment schedule for each Work Order will be structured in an effort to maintain cash neutrality for Quintiles (with respect to the payment of professional fees, pass-through costs and otherwise). Unless otherwise agreed in a particular Work Order, the following shall apply: (a) Quintiles will invoice Sponsor monthly for the fees, expenses and pass-through costs incurred in performing the Services; and, (b) Sponsor shall pay each invoice within thirty (30) days of receipt of the invoice. If any portion of an invoice is disputed, then Sponsor shall pay the undisputed amounts as set forth in the preceding sentence and the parties shall use good faith efforts to reconcile the disputed amount as soon as practicable.

suggestions.reason: The Term clause exposes Quintiles, Inc. to significant operational and financial risk because it contains no termination safeguards of its own: it does not require written notice, does not specify when termination takes effect, and does not address consequences such as payment for work performed, return of materials, or survival of key obligations, all of which are deferred without elaboration to Section 15. If Section 15 is itself incomplete or ambiguous, Quintiles, Inc. would have no express contractual basis to enforce these protections or to dispute a counterparty's unilateral characterization of the termination's scope and effect. The absence of a written notice requirement and an effective-date mechanism is particularly critical for Quintiles, Inc., as it creates uncertainty over the precise moment contractual obligations cease and exposes Quintiles, Inc. to disputes over post-termination performance and liability. Section 15 must comprehensively address termination grounds, cure periods, consequences, transition obligations, and survival of provisions to give this cross-reference operative effect.
suggestions.original_text: Term. This Agreement shall commence on the date it has been signed by all parties and shall continue for a period of five (5) years from the date of execution, unless otherwise earlier terminated by either party in accordance with Section 15 below.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted exposes Quintiles, Inc to three compounding risks: first, by requiring only generic "execution by both parties" without specifying authorized representatives, any employee or agent of Sponsor could purport to bind Sponsor to or reject a Change Order, creating disputes about validity that directly affect Quintiles' ability to recover additional budget and timeline relief; second, the amendment mechanism is limited to Work Order details and assumptions, leaving other terms of the Agreement—including schedules and other incorporated documents—potentially amendable by informal means; third, and most critically for Quintiles, the absence of an anti-oral-modification provision means Sponsor could argue that verbal instructions or a course of conduct on a Project altered Quintiles' obligations or waived Quintiles' right to insist on a formal Change Order, undermining the protection that Quintiles' reservation of rights in the final sentences of the clause is designed to provide.
suggestions.original_text: Change Orders. Any change in the details of a Work Order or the assumptions upon which the Work Order is based (including, but not limited to, changes in an agreed starting date for a Project or suspension of the Project by Sponsor) may require changes in the budget and/or timelines, and shall require a written amendment to the Work Order (a “Change Order”). Each Change Order shall detail the requested changes to the applicable task, responsibility, duty, budget, timeline or other matter. The Change Order will become effective upon the execution of the Change Order by both parties, and the parties will agree upon a reasonable period of time within which Quintiles shall implement the changes. Both parties agree to act in good faith and promptly when considering a Change Order requested by the other party. Without limiting the foregoing, Sponsor agrees that it will not unreasonably withhold approval of a Change Order, if the proposed changes in budgets or timelines result from, among other appropriate reasons, forces outside the reasonable control of Quintiles or Sponsor’s changes in the assumptions upon which the initial budget or timelines were based, including, but not limited to, the assumptions set forth in the budget or timelines. Quintiles reserves the right to postpone effecting material changes in the Project’s scope until such time as the parties agree to and execute the corresponding Change Order. For any Change Order that affects the scope of the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles, Quintiles and Sponsor shall execute a corresponding amendment to the Transfer of Obligations Form. Sponsor shall file such amendment where appropriate, or as required by law or regulation.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, this clause is entirely one-sided: it defines and protects only "Sponsor Confidential Information," leaving Quintiles, Inc. with no contractual protection for its own proprietary methodologies, systems, and data shared during performance of the Services. The clause also imposes no express standard of care on either party, meaning Quintiles, Inc. has no defined benchmark against which its handling obligations are measured, exposing it to open-ended liability for any disclosure. Additionally, the absence of a return or destruction obligation means Sponsor retains possession of Quintiles, Inc.'s information indefinitely after the Agreement ends, with no mechanism for Quintiles, Inc. to reclaim or secure its own confidential materials.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor Confidential Information. It is understood that during the course of this Agreement, Quintiles and its employees may be exposed to data and information that are confidential and proprietary to Sponsor. All such data and information (hereinafter “Sponsor Confidential Information”) written or verbal, tangible or intangible, made available, disclosed, or otherwise made known to Quintiles and its employees as a result of Services under this Agreement shall be considered confidential and shall be considered the sole property of Sponsor.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Confidential Information. It is understood that during the course of this Agreement, each party and its employees may be exposed to data and information that are confidential and proprietary to the other party. All such data and information ("Confidential Information"), written or verbal, tangible or intangible, made available, disclosed, or otherwise made known to the receiving party and its employees as a result of Services under this Agreement shall be considered confidential and the sole property of the disclosing party. Each party shall protect the other party's Confidential Information using no less than the same degree of care it uses to protect its own confidential information, but in no event less than reasonable care. Upon the written request of the disclosing party, or upon expiration or termination of this Agreement, the receiving party shall promptly return or destroy all Confidential Information of the disclosing party.

suggestions.reason: The need-to-know restriction as currently drafted does not require that employees, agents, or subcontractors of either party who receive Confidential Information are themselves bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those in this Agreement. This creates a material gap for Quintiles, Inc.: Sponsor's personnel or contractors could receive Quintiles' proprietary information on a purported "need-to-know" basis with no enforceable downstream obligation to protect it, exposing Quintiles to uncontrolled dissemination of its Confidential Information without recourse against individual recipients. The companion sentence limiting use to "employees" compounds this risk by failing to impose accountability on the receiving party for any breach by those individuals. Given the ten-year confidentiality tail tied to Work Order completion, this unaddressed gap could leave Quintiles' Confidential Information unprotected throughout a substantial post-engagement period.
suggestions.original_text: Confidentiality Obligations. For the purposes of Sections 5.3 and 5.4, Confidential Information shall mean both Sponsor Confidential Information and Quintiles Confidential Information. Each party hereunder agrees that Confidential Information disclosed by one party to the other shall be clearly marked ‘confidential’, or if disclosed orally, is confirmed in writing as having been disclosed as confidential or proprietary of the disclosing party within thirty (30) days after such disclosure. Quintiles and Sponsor each agree that it will only provide Confidential Information to the other party on a need-to-know basis and to the extent that Confidential Information is required for its undertaking of this Agreement. The Confidential Information shall be used by the receiving party and its employees only for purposes of performing the receiving party’s obligations hereunder. Except as otherwise expressly authorized in this Agreement, each party agrees that it will not make copies or duplicates of any Confidential Information, or reveal, publish or otherwise disclose the Confidential Information of the other party to any third party without the prior written consent of the disclosing party. Each party agrees that it will not disclose the terms of this Agreement or any Work Order to any third party without the written consent of the other party, which shall not unreasonably be withheld. These obligations of confidentiality and nondisclosure shall remain in effect for a period often (10) years after the completion or termination of the applicable Work Order.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Confidentiality Obligations. For the purposes of Sections 5.3 and 5.4, Confidential Information shall mean both Sponsor Confidential Information and Quintiles Confidential Information. Each party hereunder agrees that Confidential Information disclosed by one party to the other shall be clearly marked 'confidential', or if disclosed orally, is confirmed in writing as having been disclosed as confidential or proprietary of the disclosing party within thirty (30) days after such disclosure. Quintiles and Sponsor each agree that it will only disclose Confidential Information received from the other party to its own employees, agents, and subcontractors on a need-to-know basis and to the extent that such Confidential Information is required for its undertaking of this Agreement, and only to those persons who are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those set forth herein. The Confidential Information shall be used by the receiving party and its employees, agents, and subcontractors only for purposes of performing the receiving party's obligations hereunder, and the receiving party shall remain responsible for any breach of this Agreement by such persons. Except as otherwise expressly authorized in this Agreement, each party agrees that it will not make copies or duplicates of any Confidential Information, or reveal, publish or otherwise disclose the Confidential Information of the other party to any third party without the prior written consent of the disclosing party. Each party agrees that it will not disclose the terms of this Agreement or any Work Order to any third party without the written consent of the other party, which shall not unreasonably be withheld. These obligations of confidentiality and nondisclosure shall remain in effect for a period of ten (10) years after the completion or termination of the applicable Work Order.

suggestions.clause: Ownership and Inventions; No Implied Rights
suggestions.reason: The "Sponsor's Property" provision establishes Sponsor's exclusive ownership of supplied materials but is entirely silent on whether those materials may infringe third-party intellectual property rights. Because Quintiles, Inc. receives and actively uses Sponsor's Property in performing services under the Agreement, Quintiles is exposed to third-party infringement claims without any contractual protection or right of recourse against Sponsor. Without a representation from Sponsor that Sponsor's Property does not infringe third-party rights, Quintiles, Inc. bears the practical and financial risk of defending infringement claims arising from materials it did not create and has no ability to control.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor’s Property. Sponsor’s property shall mean any invention, trade secret or know-how related to or derived from any materials, documents, programs or information belonging to Sponsor and supplied to Quintiles pursuant to this Agreement, and such inventions, trade secret and know-how shall remain the exclusive property of Sponsor (collectively “Sponsor’s Property”).
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor's Property. Sponsor's property shall mean any invention, trade secret or know-how related to or derived from any materials, documents, programs or information belonging to Sponsor and supplied to Quintiles pursuant to this Agreement, and such inventions, trade secret and know-how shall remain the exclusive property of Sponsor (collectively "Sponsor's Property"). Sponsor represents and warrants that Sponsor's Property, as supplied to Quintiles, does not infringe any third-party intellectual property rights, and Sponsor shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Quintiles, Inc. against any third-party claims arising from any such infringement.

suggestions.clause: Ownership and Inventions; No Implied Rights
suggestions.reason: The license granted to Sponsor over Quintiles' Software lacks a defined term, creating a risk that Sponsor could argue the license continues indefinitely so long as it asserts the software remains "necessary" — a standard that is entirely within Sponsor's power to dispute, leaving Quintiles, Inc. without meaningful control over its proprietary software. Additionally, the permitted use is described only as "in connection with such Sponsor project under the Agreement," which is broader than the access-and-retrieval purpose that justifies the grant and could permit Sponsor to use Quintiles' Software beyond that narrow operational need. The return trigger — "no longer necessary" — is undefined and subjective, further undermining Quintiles' ability to reclaim its Software after the project concludes. These gaps could collectively expose Quintiles, Inc. to unintended, prolonged, and unchecked use of its core intellectual property assets.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor and Quintiles agree that any Quintiles’ Property or improvements thereto which are used, improved, modified or developed by Quintiles under the term of this Agreement, and which do not use or include any Sponsor Confidential Information or Sponsor’s Property, are the sole and exclusive property of Quintiles and shall be deemed Quintiles Confidential Information. To the extent the Quintiles Software (defined as programs for the purposes of data derivations, population identification, production of statistical analysis outputs, is determined to be necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data generated as a result of the Services performed by Quintiles under this Agreement, Quintiles grants to Sponsor a royalty-free, non-exclusive license with the right use by only Sponsor (and not its Affiliates or other third parties) without the right to sell, assign or sublicense such software programs and any improvements thereto in connection with such Sponsor project under the Agreement. For such software, Quintiles will provide to Sponsor the macros. When Quintiles’ Software is no longer necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data as described above, such Quintiles Software shall be returned to Quintiles.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor and Quintiles agree that any Quintiles' Property or improvements thereto which are used, improved, modified or developed by Quintiles under the term of this Agreement, and which do not use or include any Sponsor Confidential Information or Sponsor's Property, are the sole and exclusive property of Quintiles and shall be deemed Quintiles Confidential Information. To the extent the Quintiles Software (defined as programs for the purposes of data derivations, population identification, production of statistical analysis outputs) is determined to be necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data generated as a result of the Services performed by Quintiles under this Agreement, Quintiles grants to Sponsor a royalty-free, non-exclusive license, for the duration of the applicable Sponsor project under the Agreement only, with the right to use by only Sponsor (and not its Affiliates or other third parties) without the right to sell, assign or sublicense such software programs and any improvements thereto, solely for the purpose of accessing, retrieving or using the study data generated under such Sponsor project. For such software, Quintiles will provide to Sponsor the macros. When Quintiles' Software is no longer necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data as described above, or upon expiration or termination of the applicable Sponsor project under the Agreement, whichever is earlier, the license granted herein shall immediately terminate and such Quintiles Software shall be promptly returned to Quintiles.

suggestions.reason: The Records and Materials clause is entirely silent on any audit right, its permissible scope, required advance notice, frequency, cooperation obligations, correction process, and cost allocation. Without these defined parameters, Quintiles, Inc. is exposed to ad hoc, unscheduled, and potentially unlimited demands from Sponsor for access to Quintiles' records, systems, and premises, with no procedural safeguards to protect Quintiles' operations or limit disruption. The absence of cost allocation is particularly harmful to Quintiles, as Sponsor could otherwise argue that Quintiles must bear audit costs, and the lack of a correction mechanism denies Quintiles a fair opportunity to address any findings before escalation. These omissions should be addressed within this clause, and the resulting audit obligations should be read in conjunction with the confidentiality provisions referenced elsewhere in the Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: Records and Materials. Quintiles agrees to retain all records and data generated in the performance of any Project under this Agreement, and other Project-related materials including without limitation Sponsor’s proprietary compound (“Records and Materials”), and further agrees to maintain all Records and Materials in a secure area reasonably protected from fire, theft and destruction. At the completion of the Services by Quintiles, all materials, information and all other data owned by Sponsor, regardless of the method of storage or retrieval, shall be delivered to Sponsor in such form as is then currently in the possession of Quintiles, subject to the payment obligations set forth in Section 2 herein. Alternatively, at Sponsor’s option and written request, such materials and data may be (i) retained by Quintiles for Sponsor for an agreed-upon time period, or (ii) disposed of pursuant to the written directions of Sponsor. Sponsor shall pay the costs associated with any of the above options and shall pay a to-be-determined fee for storage by Quintiles of records and materials after completion or termination of the Services. Quintiles, however, reserves the right to retain, at its own cost and subject to the confidentiality provisions herein, copies of all materials that may be needed to satisfy regulatory requirements or to resolve disputes regarding the Services. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to transfer from Sponsor to Quintiles any FDA or regulatory record-keeping requirements unless such transfer is specifically provided for in the applicable Transfer of Obligations Form.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Records and Materials. Quintiles agrees to retain all records and data generated in the performance of any Project under this Agreement, and other Project-related materials including without limitation Sponsor's proprietary compound ("Records and Materials"), and further agrees to maintain all Records and Materials in a secure area reasonably protected from fire, theft and destruction. Sponsor shall have the right, upon not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice and no more than once per calendar year, to audit Quintiles' Records and Materials, relevant premises, and systems pertaining to the applicable Project; Quintiles shall cooperate with any such audit and provide reasonable access to relevant records and personnel, and shall address any material findings within a mutually agreed timeframe. Sponsor shall bear all costs of any such audit. At the completion of the Services by Quintiles, all materials, information and all other data owned by Sponsor, regardless of the method of storage or retrieval, shall be delivered to Sponsor in such form as is then currently in the possession of Quintiles, subject to the payment obligations set forth in Section 2 herein. Alternatively, at Sponsor's option and written request, such materials and data may be (i) retained by Quintiles for Sponsor for an agreed-upon time period, or (ii) disposed of pursuant to the written directions of Sponsor. Sponsor shall pay the costs associated with any of the above options and shall pay a to-be-determined fee for storage by Quintiles of records and materials after completion or termination of the Services. Quintiles, however, reserves the right to retain, at its own cost and subject to the confidentiality provisions herein, copies of all materials that may be needed to satisfy regulatory requirements or to resolve disputes regarding the Services. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to transfer from Sponsor to Quintiles any FDA or regulatory record-keeping requirements unless such transfer is specifically provided for in the applicable Transfer of Obligations Form.

suggestions.reason: The clause correctly disclaims partnership, agency, and employment relationships but omits two foundational elements of an independent contractor provision: a statement that each party controls the manner and means by which its own personnel perform work, and an allocation of responsibility for personnel-related costs, taxes, and benefits. For Quintiles, Inc., these omissions create meaningful exposure to tax authority or labor law reclassification challenges, as a court or regulator may decline to treat the relationship as independent contracting where the agreement itself is silent on control and financial responsibility. If Quintiles, Inc.'s personnel were recharacterized as employees of the counterparty, or if Quintiles, Inc. were held jointly liable for the counterparty's payroll or withholding obligations, the financial and operational consequences could be significant.
suggestions.original_text: Independent Contractor Relationship. For the purposes of this Agreement, the parties hereto are independent contractors and nothing contained in this Agreement shall be construed to place them in the relationship of partners, principal and agent, employer/employee or joint venturers. Neither party shall have the power or right to bind or obligate the other party, and neither party shall hold itself out as having such authority.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Independent Contractor Relationship. For the purposes of this Agreement, the parties hereto are independent contractors, each of which shall control the manner and means by which its own personnel perform work under this Agreement, and nothing contained in this Agreement shall be construed to place them in the relationship of partners, principal and agent, employer/employee or joint venturers. Each party shall be solely responsible for all compensation, benefits, taxes, and withholdings applicable to its own personnel. Neither party shall have the power or right to bind or obligate the other party, and neither party shall hold itself out as having such authority.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted exposes Quintiles, Inc. to material compliance risk in three respects: it contains no commitment by either party to anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws, leaving Quintiles with no contractual protection should Sponsor-side conduct implicate Quintiles in a violation; it contains no obligation on either party to notify the other of a material legal breach affecting performance, meaning Quintiles could unknowingly continue performing under a compromised regulatory posture; and it is entirely silent on forced labor, child labor, and human trafficking in Quintiles' supply chain, a gap that creates reputational and regulatory exposure for Quintiles as more jurisdictions extend supply-chain due-diligence obligations to service providers. If left unaddressed, these omissions could expose Quintiles to regulatory sanction, enforcement liability, and reputational harm without any contractual mechanism to surface or remediate the underlying issues.
suggestions.original_text: Quintiles agrees that its Services will be conducted in compliance with all applicable laws, rules and regulations, including but not limited to the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act and the regulations promulgated pursuant thereto, and with the standard of care customary in the contract research organization industry. Regarding the FDA’s electronic records and signatures regulation, 21 CFR Part 11 (“Part 11”), Quintiles has a compliance plan in place as to its applicable database applications and electronic records systems and it is working diligently to implement its plan. Quintiles, however, is not responsible for the compliance or non-compliance of applications or systems used by third parties (including, but not limited to, investigative sites or third party laboratories), or any Part 11 audits or assessments thereof, unless such applications or systems are owned by Quintiles. Quintiles’ standard operating procedures will be used in performance of the Services, unless otherwise specifically stated in the Work Order. Sponsor represents that it will cooperate with Quintiles in taking any actions that Quintiles and Sponsor reasonably believes are necessary to comply with the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles hereunder.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Quintiles agrees that its Services will be conducted in compliance with all applicable laws, rules and regulations, including but not limited to the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act and the regulations promulgated pursuant thereto, applicable anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws, and laws prohibiting forced labor, child labor, and human trafficking in its supply chain, and with the standard of care customary in the contract research organization industry. Regarding the FDA's electronic records and signatures regulation, 21 CFR Part 11 ("Part 11"), Quintiles has a compliance plan in place as to its applicable database applications and electronic records systems and it is working diligently to implement its plan. Quintiles, however, is not responsible for the compliance or non-compliance of applications or systems used by third parties (including, but not limited to, investigative sites or third party laboratories), or any Part 11 audits or assessments thereof, unless such applications or systems are owned by Quintiles. Quintiles' standard operating procedures will be used in performance of the Services, unless otherwise specifically stated in the Work Order. Sponsor represents that it will cooperate with Quintiles in taking any actions that Quintiles and Sponsor reasonably believes are necessary to comply with the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles hereunder. Each party shall promptly notify the other in writing upon becoming aware of any material breach of applicable law or regulation affecting its performance of obligations under this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, this clause imposes a unilateral representation and a continuing forward-looking covenant exclusively on Quintiles, Inc., with no corresponding obligation on Sponsor, exposing Quintiles to uncapped liability for any breach of the warranty or covenant while Sponsor bears no equivalent risk. The phrase "in any way prevent" is impermissibly broad and undefined, meaning that even a theoretical, immaterial impediment to service delivery could constitute a breach, giving Sponsor a broad trigger to claim damages or allege warranty failure without any de minimis threshold. The absence of a materiality qualifier compounds this risk, as Quintiles, Inc. could face liability for breach in circumstances where Sponsor's own conduct, delays, or failures contributed to the inability to provide the Services. Making the clause mutual and introducing a materiality standard brings the provision to market equilibrium and limits Quintiles, Inc.'s exposure to genuinely consequential conflicts.
suggestions.original_text: Conflict of Agreements. Quintiles represents to Sponsor that it is not a party to any agreement which would prevent it from fulfilling its obligations under this Agreement and that during the term of this Agreement, Quintiles agrees that it will not enter into any agreement to provide services which would in any way prevent it from providing the Services contemplated under this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Conflict of Agreements. Each party represents to the other that it is not a party to any agreement which would prevent it from fulfilling its material obligations under this Agreement and that during the term of this Agreement, each party agrees that it will not enter into any agreement that would materially prevent it from fulfilling its respective obligations under this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The publication restriction in its current form is entirely one-sided: it prohibits only Quintiles and its affiliates from publishing or referring to project data or results without Sponsor's consent, while imposing no equivalent restriction on Sponsor, leaving Quintiles, Inc. with no contractual protection against unauthorized publication by Sponsor. Additionally, the clause contains no carve-out for disclosures required by applicable law or regulation, meaning Quintiles, Inc. could be held in breach if compelled by a regulator, court, or legal process to disclose project data, creating material compliance and litigation exposure. The name-use restriction in the second sentence also omits logos and trademarks, leaving Quintiles, Inc.'s broader intellectual property inadequately protected against unauthorized use in promotions or publications.
suggestions.original_text: Publication; Use of Name. Project data or results may not be published or referred to, in whole or in part, by Quintiles or its affiliates without the prior expressed written consent of Sponsor. Neither party will use the other party’s name in connection with any publication or promotion without the other party’s prior, written consent.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the exclusion of consequential, indirect, and special losses applies solely to Quintiles and its personnel, with no equivalent restriction binding Sponsor — meaning Quintiles' protection could be challenged as an unenforceable one-sided clause, leaving Quintiles, Inc. exposed to full consequential damages claims if a court declines to give effect to the asymmetric exclusion. More critically, the clause purports to exclude "any liability of any type," including for negligence and tort, with no carve-out for fraud, willful misconduct, death, or personal injury caused by negligence; this absolute formulation is unenforceable in most jurisdictions and risks the entire limitation provision being struck down, eliminating Quintiles, Inc.'s aggregate cap protection entirely. If the cap is voided, Quintiles, Inc.'s financial exposure under this Agreement and all Work Orders becomes unlimited, a material operational and financial risk. A standard market carve-out for these uncappable heads of liability must be added, and the consequential loss exclusion should be made mutual, to preserve the enforceability of the clause as a whole.
suggestions.original_text: Limitation of Liability. Neither Quintiles, nor its affiliates, nor any of Quintiles’ or its affiliate’s directors, officers, employees, subcontractors or agents shall have any liability of any type (including, but not limited to, contract, negligence, and tort liability), for any loss of profits, opportunity or goodwill, or any type of special, incidental, indirect or consequential damage or loss in connection with or arising out of this Agreement, any Work Order, or the Services performed by Quintiles hereunder. In addition, in no event shall the collective, aggregate liability (including, but not limited to, contract, negligence and tort liability) of Quintiles or its affiliates, or Quintiles’ or its affiliates’ directors, officers, employees, subcontractors and agents, under this Agreement or any Work Order hereunder exceed the amount of fees actually received by Quintiles from Sponsor for the assignment or task from which such liability arose.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Limitation of Liability. Neither party, nor its affiliates, nor any of their respective directors, officers, employees, subcontractors or agents shall have any liability of any type (including, but not limited to, contract, negligence, and tort liability), for any loss of profits, opportunity or goodwill, or any type of special, incidental, indirect or consequential damage or loss in connection with or arising out of this Agreement, any Work Order, or the Services performed by Quintiles hereunder. In addition, in no event shall the collective, aggregate liability (including, but not limited to, contract, negligence and tort liability) of Quintiles or its affiliates, or Quintiles' or its affiliates' directors, officers, employees, subcontractors and agents, under this Agreement or any Work Order hereunder exceed the amount of fees actually received by Quintiles from Sponsor for the assignment or task from which such liability arose. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Section, nothing herein shall limit or exclude either party's liability for fraud, willful misconduct, or death or personal injury caused by that party's negligence.

suggestions.reason: The aggregate liability cap in this Agreement, as evidenced by the operative language, is drafted exclusively to limit Quintiles' exposure and does not cap Sponsor's liability on a reciprocal basis, leaving Quintiles, Inc. exposed to uncapped claims from Sponsor in the same circumstances where Quintiles' own recovery is capped. This one-sided structure is commercially unfair to Quintiles and creates material financial risk. Additionally, the clause contains no carve-outs preserving uncapped exposure for either party's breach of confidentiality, data breach, infringement of intellectual property rights, or indemnification obligations—categories that market-standard agreements routinely exclude from general liability caps given their potentially catastrophic and difficult-to-quantify nature. The absence of such carve-outs means Quintiles' ability to pursue full recovery against Sponsor for, among other things, a data or confidentiality breach is effectively curtailed by the same cap that limits Quintiles' own liability.
suggestions.original_text: EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY REPRESENTATION OR WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, ANY WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE OR NON-INFRINGEMENT OF A PATENT, TRADEMARK OR OTHER INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHT.
suggestions.suggested_fix: EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY REPRESENTATION OR WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, ANY WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE OR NON-INFRINGEMENT OF A PATENT, TRADEMARK OR OTHER INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHT. THE AGGREGATE LIABILITY CAP SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT SHALL APPLY EQUALLY AND RECIPROCALLY TO BOTH QUINTILES AND SPONSOR. NOTWITHSTANDING ANY OTHER PROVISION OF THIS AGREEMENT, SUCH CAP SHALL NOT APPLY TO EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING FROM BREACH OF CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS, UNAUTHORIZED DISCLOSURE OR BREACH OF DATA SECURITY, INFRINGEMENT OF INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS, OR OBLIGATIONS OF INDEMNIFICATION UNDER THIS AGREEMENT.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the indemnification clause contains no claims-handling mechanics, meaning Quintiles, Inc. has no contractual assurance that it retains prompt notice rights, the ability to control or meaningfully participate in its own defense, or Sponsor's consent before any settlement is entered that could bind Quintiles. Without a provision clarifying that indemnification obligations are excluded from any limitation of liability cap elsewhere in the Agreement, Sponsor could argue that its indemnity exposure is capped, leaving Quintiles, Inc. with uncovered Losses on significant third-party claims. The absence of a mitigation obligation also leaves the clause susceptible to challenge as overreaching, potentially undermining its enforceability to Quintiles' detriment. Any limitation of liability provision in this Agreement should be reviewed to confirm that the carve-out added below is consistent with its terms.
suggestions.original_text: Indemnification. Sponsor shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Quintiles and its affiliates, and its and their directors, officers, employees and agents (each, a “Quintiles Indemnified Party”), from and against any and all losses, damages, liabilities, reasonable attorney fees, court costs, and expenses (collectively “Losses”), joint or several, resulting or arising from any third-party claims, actions, proceedings, investigations or litigation relating to or arising from or in connection with this Agreement, any Work Order, or the Services contemplated herein (including, without limitation, any Losses arising from or in connection with any study, test, device, product or potential product to which this Agreement or any Work Order relates), except to the extent such Losses are determined to have resulted solely from the negligence or intentional misconduct of a Quintiles Indemnified Party seeking indemnity hereunder. Quintiles shall indemnify and hold harmless Sponsor, its affiliates and their respective directors, officers, employees and agents harmless from and against any Losses arising from the negligence or intentional misconduct of a Quintiles Indemnified Party.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted is purely procedural and contains no substantive indemnification obligation: it identifies no trigger events, specifies no covered losses, and does not state which party owes an indemnity to which, leaving Quintiles, Inc. without an enforceable right to claim indemnification at all. The absence of mutuality language and any relationship to the Agreement's liability caps creates the further risk that a counterparty could argue that any indemnity is uncapped or, conversely, that no indemnity obligation exists independent of this procedural paragraph. Without a mitigation requirement, Quintiles, Inc. is exposed to escalating loss claims with no corresponding duty on the indemnified party to limit its exposure. These gaps collectively create material financial and legal risk for Quintiles, Inc. and should be aligned with the Agreement's limitation of liability provisions to establish a coherent liability framework.
suggestions.original_text: Indemnification Procedure. Any party seeking indemnity hereunder shall (a) give prompt notice to the other party (the “Indemnifying Party”) of any such claim or lawsuit (including a copy thereof) served upon it, (b) permit the Indemnifying Party to assume full responsibility to investigate, prepare for, and defend against such claim or lawsuit, (c) shall fully cooperate with the Indemnifying Party and its legal representatives in the investigation of any matter the subject of indemnification, and (d) shall not compromise or settle such claim or lawsuit in a manner that adversely affects the other party’s rights under this Agreement without the Indemnifying Party’s prior written consent. The party seeking indemnity shall not unreasonably withhold its approval of the settlement of any claim, liability, or action covered by this Indemnification provision.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the termination clause grants Sponsor a unilateral right to exit without cause on thirty (30) days' notice while affording Quintiles, Inc. no reciprocal right to terminate, leaving Quintiles commercially exposed with no equivalent exit mechanism. The clause is also silent on transition assistance obligations, the period and fees applicable to such assistance, survival of material provisions, and any requirement for Sponsor to cooperate with a replacement provider — gaps that could leave Quintiles performing uncompensated work, bound by obligations that have no post-termination anchor, and without leverage to manage an orderly wind-down of Services. These omissions create concrete financial and operational risk for Quintiles, Inc., particularly where a Work Order is mid-performance and significant costs have been incurred. The survival gap should be aligned with any separate survival clause in the Agreement; if none exists, the provisions identified below provide a minimum protective floor.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order without cause at any time during the term of the Agreement on thirty (30) day’s prior written notice to Quintiles.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order without cause at any time during the term of the Agreement on thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other party. Following the effective date of termination, Quintiles shall provide reasonable transition assistance for up to sixty (60) days at its then-current rates, and Sponsor shall cooperate with any replacement provider designated by Quintiles. All provisions relating to payment of accrued fees, confidentiality, intellectual property, indemnification, and limitation of liability shall survive expiration or termination of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The clause requires the parties to "promptly meet to prepare a close-out schedule" but imposes no deadline on when that meeting must occur, no minimum content requirements for the close-out schedule, and no obligation on the counterparty to cooperate in an orderly transition. For Quintiles, this creates meaningful operational and financial exposure: without a defined timeline and scope for the close-out schedule, the counterparty could delay or dispute the wind-down process, leaving Quintiles performing residual Services without clear payment entitlement or defined handover obligations. The absence of an express transition assistance requirement also means Quintiles has no contractual basis to enforce cooperative wind-down conduct if the counterparty fails to engage constructively after a breach-triggered termination.
suggestions.original_text: Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order for material breach upon thirty (30) days’ written notice specifying the nature of the breach, if such breach has not been substantially cured within the thirty (30) day period. During the 30-day cure period for termination due to breach, each party will continue to perform its obligations under the Agreement. If the cure period has expired without a substantial cure of the breach, then the parties shall promptly meet to prepare a close-out schedule, and Quintiles shall cease performing all work not necessary for the orderly close-out of the Services or required by laws or regulations.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order for material breach upon thirty (30) days' written notice specifying the nature of the breach, if such breach has not been substantially cured within the thirty (30) day period. During the 30-day cure period for termination due to breach, each party will continue to perform its obligations under the Agreement. If the cure period has expired without a substantial cure of the breach, then the parties shall meet within five (5) Business Days following expiration of the cure period to prepare a close-out schedule, which shall address the orderly handover of work product and materials, payment for all Services performed through the close-out date, and any transition assistance reasonably necessary to minimize disruption, and Quintiles shall cease performing all work not necessary for the orderly close-out of the Services or required by laws or regulations.

suggestions.reason: The catch-all limb of the "control" definition — "otherwise having the ability to influence and direct the polices and direction of an entity" — is substantively vague and contains a typographical error ("polices" for "policies"), both of which expose Quintiles, Inc. to material risk. Because "influence" is a markedly lower threshold than actual legal or contractual control, Sponsor could argue that entities Quintiles merely influences (e.g., minority investees, joint ventures, or strategic partners) qualify as Quintiles affiliates, thereby binding those entities to the Agreement's obligations and extending Quintiles' performance liability across a wider corporate network than intended. Replacing the undefined, subjective standard with the market-standard formulation — "the power to direct the management and policies of an entity, whether through ownership, by contract, or otherwise" — provides an objective, enforceable threshold that protects Quintiles, Inc. from inadvertent over-inclusion of entities outside its actual control.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor agrees that Quintiles may use the Services of its corporate affiliates to fulfill Quintiles’ obligations under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any affiliate so used shall be subject to all of the terms and conditions applicable to Quintiles under this Agreement or any Work Order, and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Quintiles under this Agreement and any Work Order. Quintiles agrees that Sponsor’s affiliates may use the services of Quintiles (and its affiliates) under this Agreement. In such event, such Sponsor’s affiliates shall be bound by all the terms and conditions of this Agreement and any Work Order and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Sponsor under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any such affiliate of Sponsor or Quintiles may execute a Work Order directly. The term “affiliate” shall mean all entities controlling, controlled by or under common control with Sponsor or Quintiles, as the case may be. The term “control” shall mean the ability to vote fifty percent (50%) or more of the voting securities of any entity or otherwise having the ability to influence and direct the polices and direction of an entity.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor agrees that Quintiles may use the Services of its corporate affiliates to fulfill Quintiles' obligations under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any affiliate so used shall be subject to all of the terms and conditions applicable to Quintiles under this Agreement or any Work Order, and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Quintiles under this Agreement and any Work Order. Quintiles agrees that Sponsor's affiliates may use the services of Quintiles (and its affiliates) under this Agreement. In such event, such Sponsor's affiliates shall be bound by all the terms and conditions of this Agreement and any Work Order and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Sponsor under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any such affiliate of Sponsor or Quintiles may execute a Work Order directly. The term "affiliate" shall mean all entities controlling, controlled by or under common control with Sponsor or Quintiles, as the case may be. The term "control" shall mean the ability to vote fifty percent (50%) or more of the voting securities of any entity or otherwise having the power to direct the management and policies of an entity, whether through ownership, by contract, or otherwise.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, condition (i) grants Sponsor an unconstrained prior written approval right over Quintiles' subcontracting decisions, with no obligation on Sponsor to respond within a defined period and no standard limiting how or whether that approval may be withheld. This exposes Quintiles, Inc. to material operational and schedule risk: Sponsor could indefinitely delay or arbitrarily refuse approval, yet Quintiles remains fully liable under condition (ii) for all Project obligations. The commercial asymmetry is significant — Quintiles bears the entire subcontracting liability burden while Sponsor holds an unqualified veto that could be used to impede performance or extract concessions, without any corresponding obligation or accountability. Adding a reasonableness qualifier to Sponsor's approval right directly addresses this imbalance while preserving Sponsor's legitimate interest in evaluating proposed subcontractors.
suggestions.original_text: Quintiles shall have the right to subcontract a portion of its obligations in connection with its performance of any Project (other than to its corporate affiliates), provided that (i) Quintiles shall have obtained the prior written approval of Sponsor to the subcontract, including providing Sponsor with sufficient information to enable proper evaluation of such subcontractor; (ii) such subcontract shall not relieve Quintiles of any of its obligations under this Agreement; (iii) Quintiles shall enter into a written agreement with each subcontractor on terms and conditions consistent with this Agreement, including for the benefit of Sponsor, provisions substantially similar to those of Sections 5.0,6.0, and 11.0; (iv) each Work Order, when appropriate, shall specify the name of such subcontractors; and (v) if requested by Sponsor, Quintiles agrees to provide Sponsor with a copy of each such subcontract.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Quintiles shall have the right to subcontract a portion of its obligations in connection with its performance of any Project (other than to its corporate affiliates), provided that (i) Quintiles shall have obtained the prior written approval of Sponsor to the subcontract, such approval not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, including providing Sponsor with sufficient information to enable proper evaluation of such subcontractor; (ii) such subcontract shall not relieve Quintiles of any of its obligations under this Agreement; (iii) Quintiles shall enter into a written agreement with each subcontractor on terms and conditions consistent with this Agreement, including for the benefit of Sponsor, provisions substantially similar to those of Sections 5.0, 6.0, and 11.0; (iv) each Work Order, when appropriate, shall specify the name of such subcontractors; and (v) if requested by Sponsor, Quintiles agrees to provide Sponsor with a copy of each such subcontract.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "in a timely manner" governing Sponsor's obligation to deliver documents, materials, and information to Quintiles is not anchored to any objective deadline, leaving Quintiles, Inc. exposed to Sponsor-caused delays with no clear contractual trigger to invoke the exculpatory protections in the final sentence of this clause. Without a defined delivery standard, Sponsor could dispute whether its delivery was timely, undermining Quintiles, Inc.'s ability to demonstrate that a delay originated with Sponsor rather than Quintiles, Inc. This creates material financial and reputational risk for Quintiles, Inc. where project timelines slip and Sponsor attempts to attribute responsibility to Quintiles, Inc. under the relevant Work Order or Change Order. Anchoring Sponsor's delivery obligation to the timelines established in the applicable Work Order or Change Order is consistent with the existing framework and provides Quintiles, Inc. with an objective, enforceable benchmark.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor shall forward to Quintiles in a timely manner all documents, materials and information in Sponsor’s possession or control necessary for Quintiles to conduct the Services. Quintiles will use commercially reasonable efforts to complete the agreed upon Services within the timelines set forth in an executed Work Order or Change Order. Quintiles shall not be liable to Sponsor nor be deemed to have breached this Agreement for errors, delays or other consequences arising from Sponsor’s failure to timely provide documents, materials or information or to otherwise cooperate with Quintiles in order for Quintiles to timely and properly perform its obligations under the relevant Work Order or Change Order.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor shall forward to Quintiles in accordance with the timelines set forth in the applicable Work Order or Change Order, or if no timeline is specified therein, within five (5) Business Days of a written request by Quintiles, all documents, materials and information in Sponsor's possession or control necessary for Quintiles to conduct the Services. Quintiles will use commercially reasonable efforts to complete the agreed upon Services within the timelines set forth in an executed Work Order or Change Order. Quintiles shall not be liable to Sponsor nor be deemed to have breached this Agreement for errors, delays or other consequences arising from Sponsor's failure to provide documents, materials or information within the timeframes required hereunder or to otherwise cooperate with Quintiles in order for Quintiles to timely and properly perform its obligations under the relevant Work Order or Change Order.

suggestions.reason: The obligation to "use good faith efforts to negotiate an acceptable resolution" imposes no objective or measurable standard on either party, exposing Quintiles, Inc. to a dispute in which a court would need extrinsic evidence to determine whether Quintiles, Inc. discharged its obligation or whether the counterparty's refusal to agree was itself a breach. Because "acceptable resolution" is entirely subjective, Sponsor could contend that any resolution Quintiles, Inc. proposed was unacceptable, effectively holding Quintiles, Inc. in perpetual negotiation without recourse. Replacing "good faith efforts" with "commercially reasonable efforts" anchors the obligation to an objective, judicially recognised standard and reduces Quintiles, Inc.'s litigation exposure if the resolution process breaks down.
suggestions.original_text: Quintiles and Sponsor agree to notify the other in writing immediately if any delays or limits are encountered in their performance of any Work Order, and shall use good faith efforts to negotiate an acceptable resolution to such delays or limits.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Quintiles and Sponsor agree to notify the other in writing immediately if any delays or limits are encountered in their performance of any Work Order, and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to negotiate and agree in writing upon a resolution to such delays or limits.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Quintiles' storage and handling obligations extend not only to applicable laws and regulations but also to any written instructions unilaterally issued by Sponsor, without any reasonableness qualifier or safeguard against instructions that conflict with applicable law or are operationally impracticable. This exposes Quintiles to open-ended, Sponsor-dictated compliance obligations that could require costly operational changes at any time and at Quintiles' expense, with no corresponding limitation on Sponsor's discretion. The absence of a reasonableness standard creates a particularly acute risk for Quintiles where Sponsor's instructions are inconsistent with governing regulatory requirements, since Quintiles would face an irreconcilable conflict with no contractual protection. This imbalance is commercially unjustified given that Sponsor already carries an express obligation to provide hazard information and to comply with applicable shipment legislation.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor shall provide Quintiles with all information available to it regarding known or potential hazards associated with the use of any substances supplied to Quintiles by Sponsor, and Sponsor shall comply with all current legislation and regulations concerning the shipment of substances by the land, sea or air. Quintiles agrees to comply with all laws, rules and regulations, including written instructions provided by Sponsor, relating to the storage and handling of any such substances received from Sponsor.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor shall provide Quintiles with all information available to it regarding known or potential hazards associated with the use of any substances supplied to Quintiles by Sponsor, and Sponsor shall comply with all current legislation and regulations concerning the shipment of substances by the land, sea or air. Quintiles agrees to comply with all laws, rules and regulations, including reasonable written instructions provided by Sponsor that do not conflict with applicable law, relating to the storage and handling of any such substances received from Sponsor.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the Force Majeure clause exposes Quintiles, Inc. to significant operational and financial risk because it imposes no notice obligation on the counterparty, no duty to mitigate or resume performance, and no termination right for Quintiles, Inc. if performance remains suspended indefinitely. The absence of a carve-out for events attributable to the affected party's own acts or omissions further allows the counterparty to shield avoidable failures — including self-caused supply chain or labour disruptions — behind a broad "beyond that party's control" standard, leaving Quintiles, Inc. with no recourse and no exit. Without a cap on the suspension period, Quintiles, Inc. could be locked into a non-performing agreement with no remedy for an unlimited time.
suggestions.original_text: Force Majeure. In the event either party shall be delayed or hindered in or prevented from the performance of any act required hereunder by reasons of strike, lockouts, labor troubles, inability to procure materials or services, failure of power or restrictive government or judicial orders, or decrees, riots, insurrection, war, Acts of God, inclement weather or other reason or cause beyond that party’s control, then performance of such act (except for the payment of money owed) shall be excused for the period of such delay.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Force Majeure. In the event either party shall be delayed or hindered in or prevented from the performance of any act required hereunder by reasons of strike, lockouts, labor troubles, inability to procure materials or services, failure of power or restrictive government or judicial orders, or decrees, riots, insurrection, war, Acts of God, inclement weather or other cause beyond that party's reasonable control and not attributable to that party's acts or omissions, then performance of such act (except for the payment of money owed) shall be excused for the period of such delay, provided that the affected party promptly notifies the other party in writing of the occurrence and expected duration of such event, uses commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate its effects and resume performance, and, if such delay continues for more than thirty (30) days, the non-affected party may terminate this Agreement upon written notice.

suggestions.reason: The notices block identifies Quintiles, Inc.'s current address and designated contact but contains no mechanism for updating those details, meaning any change of address, successor contact, or office relocation by Quintiles, Inc. would have no contractual effect and the counterparty could continue sending notices to a stale address while arguing valid delivery. This exposes Quintiles, Inc. to the practical risk of missing time-sensitive notices—including notices of breach, termination, or indemnity claims—because no procedure exists to substitute the current details. A single-sentence update mechanism is market standard and resolves the gap without altering any other provision.
suggestions.original_text: If to Quintiles: Quintiles, Inc., 10245 Hickman Mills Drive, Kansas City, MO 64137, Attn: Michael J. Baltezor, Ph.D., General Manager
suggestions.suggested_fix: If to Quintiles: Quintiles, Inc., 10245 Hickman Mills Drive, Kansas City, MO 64137, Attn: Michael J. Baltezor, Ph.D., General Manager. Either party may change its notice details by providing written notice of such change to the other party, effective ten (10) days following receipt of such notice.

suggestions.reason: The clause omits a tail-coverage period following expiration or termination, which creates a material gap for Quintiles, Inc. because Professional Liability policies are typically written on a claims-made basis and claims arising from work performed during the term may be filed after the Agreement ends, leaving Quintiles, Inc. exposed without an express run-off requirement. The General Liability obligation in item 2) is also unattributed, creating ambiguity as to whether it binds both parties equally. Most critically, the clause contains no statement that the prescribed insurance minimums do not cap or otherwise limit a party's liability, which means Sponsor could contend that the US$10,000,000.00 figure sets a ceiling on Quintiles, Inc.'s recoverable damages, undermining the Agreement's broader liability framework.
suggestions.original_text: Insurance. During the term of this Agreement to cover its obligations hereunder, each party shall maintain insurance coverage as follows: 1) (a) Professional Liability for Quintiles in an amount of at least US$10,000,000.00; (b) Product Liability for Sponsor in an amount of at least US$10,000,000.00; and 2) General Liability in amounts of at least US$3,000,000.00. All insurance amounts may be obtained by full, individual primary policy amount; a primary amount of less than minimum requirement enhanced by a blanket excess umbrella policy; or a combination of either. Each party shall provide the other party with a certificate of insurance upon request. The insured shall provide the other party with at least thirty (30) days prior written notice of any material change, cancellation or expiration of the above-required insurance.

suggestions.reason: The clause exposes Quintiles, Inc. to material financial and enforcement risk on three fronts. First, the mandate that "a currency exchange provision shall be included in the Work Order" is entirely undefined — it specifies no minimum content, assigns no drafting obligation to either party, and provides no fallback if Sponsor refuses to agree, leaving Quintiles without enforceable currency protection on high-value international Work Orders. Second, the pass-through cost reimbursement provision specifies the applicable exchange rate date but omits any deadline for Sponsor's actual payment, allowing Sponsor to delay reimbursement indefinitely after the rate is determined. Third, the $500,000 threshold means Quintiles bears uncapped foreign exchange risk on all sub-threshold Work Orders with no contractual remedy. These gaps collectively allow Sponsor to avoid or defer its currency reimbursement obligations to Quintiles' financial detriment.
suggestions.original_text: Foreign Currency Exchange. The currency to be used for invoice and payment shall be the currency stated in the Budget or Table attached to the Work Order (the “Contracted Currency”). If Quintiles incurs pass-through costs in a currency other than the Contracted Currency, then Sponsor shall reimburse Quintiles for Quintiles’ actual costs in the Contracted Currency based on the Oanda foreign currency exchange rate (Oanda.com) for the applicable currencies on the last business Friday of the month. For Work Orders that involve the performance of Services by Quintiles or its affiliates in any countries that use currencies other than the Contracted Currency, and the fees for such Services will exceed $500,000, then a currency exchange provision shall be included in the Work Order.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Foreign Currency Exchange. The currency to be used for invoice and payment shall be the currency stated in the Budget or Table attached to the Work Order (the "Contracted Currency"). If Quintiles incurs pass-through costs in a currency other than the Contracted Currency, Sponsor shall reimburse Quintiles for Quintiles' actual costs in the Contracted Currency based on the Oanda foreign currency exchange rate (Oanda.com) for the applicable currencies on the last business Friday of the month in which such costs were incurred, within thirty (30) days following receipt of Quintiles' invoice therefor. For Work Orders involving the performance of Services by Quintiles or its affiliates in countries using currencies other than the Contracted Currency, where the fees for such Services will exceed $500,000, Quintiles shall propose, and the parties shall negotiate in good faith and agree upon, a currency exchange provision to be included in the Work Order; provided that if the parties fail to agree within fifteen (15) days of Quintiles' proposal, the Oanda-based reimbursement mechanism set forth above shall apply to such Work Order.

suggestions.reason: The clause exposes Quintiles, Inc. to enforcement disputes on two fronts: first, "at the beginning of each calendar year" does not identify a specific effective date or require advance notice, leaving the counterparty room to contest when any increase actually takes effect and potentially withholding payment of adjusted fees; second, the inflation formula's use of "or" between the 4% floor and the Economist index is ambiguous as to which measure governs, allowing the counterparty to insist on whichever figure produces the lower increase and thereby eroding Quintiles' ability to recover its full rising business costs. Additionally, "the equivalent inflation index of the country where services are performed" is undefined, creating a further basis for a counterparty to dispute the applicable measure entirely and block or delay Quintiles' fee adjustment. These combined ambiguities materially undermine Quintiles' ability to exercise and enforce a right that is fundamental to the commercial viability of multi-year engagements.
suggestions.original_text: Inflation Adjustments. Where services in a Work Order are provided by Quintiles over multiple calendar years, Quintiles may increase its fees at the beginning of each calendar year to reflect increases in Quintiles’ business costs on a prospective basis only. Quintiles’ overall costs may be increased for the next twelve (12) month period using four percent (4%) or the average percentage change in the wages/earnings survey as published in the Economist (or as reported at www.economist.com) or the equivalent inflation index of the country where services are performed, over the preceding twelve (12) month period.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Inflation Adjustments. Where services in a Work Order are provided by Quintiles over multiple calendar years, Quintiles may increase its fees effective January 1 of each applicable calendar year, upon not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer, to reflect increases in Quintiles' business costs on a prospective basis only. Quintiles' overall costs may be increased for the next twelve (12) month period using the higher of four percent (4%) or the average percentage change in the wages/earnings survey as published in the Economist (or as reported at www.economist.com), or, for services performed outside the United States, the higher of four percent (4%) or the equivalent nationally recognized official inflation index published by the government or central bank of the country where services are performed, in each case over the preceding twelve (12) month period.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the assignment clause exposes Quintiles, Inc. to material operational and financial risk on several fronts: consent to any assignment is unqualified, meaning Sponsor could unreasonably withhold approval of a Quintiles corporate reorganization, affiliate transfer, or M&A transaction without recourse or time limit. The clause is also silent on the assigning party's continuing liability, leaving Quintiles potentially unable to pursue the original Sponsor obligor if Sponsor transfers its payment or other obligations to a less creditworthy entity. Critically, there is no change-of-control mechanism, so if Sponsor is acquired by a competitor of Quintiles, Quintiles has no contractual right to terminate, nor is Sponsor required to notify Quintiles of such an event. These gaps, taken together, create significant enforceability and counterparty-credit risk for Quintiles across the life of the Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: Binding Agreement and Assignment. This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of Sponsor and Quintiles and their respective successors and permitted assigns. Except as stated above in Section 17.1, neither party may assign any of its rights or obligations under this Agreement to any party without the express, written consent of the other party.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Binding Agreement and Assignment. This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of Sponsor and Quintiles and their respective successors and permitted assigns. Except as stated above in Section 17.1, neither party may assign any of its rights or obligations under this Agreement without the express, written consent of the other party, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed; provided that either party may assign this Agreement without consent to an Affiliate or in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, upon prior written notice to the non-assigning party, and in each such case the assigning party shall remain liable for all of its obligations under this Agreement unless expressly released in writing by the other party. Either party may terminate this Agreement upon written notice if the other party undergoes a change of control with a direct competitor of the terminating party.

suggestions.clause: Choice of Law, Waiver and Enforceability
suggestions.reason: The waiver provision does not require waivers to be in writing and signed by the waiving party, which creates a material risk for Quintiles, Inc. Without that formal requirement, a counterparty could argue that Quintiles, Inc.'s course of conduct, oral communications, or failure to object in a particular instance constituted an effective waiver of a material contractual right. This exposes Quintiles, Inc. to the loss of key protections—such as payment obligations, intellectual property rights, or service-level remedies—based on informal or inadvertent conduct rather than a deliberate, documented decision. A written and signed waiver requirement is a market-standard safeguard that prevents such arguments and preserves Quintiles, Inc.'s full contractual position.
suggestions.original_text: Choice of Law, Waiver and Enforceability. This Agreement shall be construed, governed, interpreted, and applied in accordance with the laws of the State of New York exclusive of its conflicts of law provisions. The failure to enforce any right or provision herein shall not constitute a waiver of that right or provision. Any waiver of a breach of a provision shall not constitute a waiver of any subsequent breach of that provision. If any provisions herein are found to be unenforceable on the grounds that they are overly broad or in conflict with applicable laws, it is the intent of the parties that such provisions be replaced, reformed or narrowed so that their original business purpose can be accomplished to the extent permitted by law, and that the remaining provisions shall not in any way be affected or impaired thereby.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Choice of Law, Waiver and Enforceability. This Agreement shall be construed, governed, interpreted, and applied in accordance with the laws of the State of New York exclusive of its conflicts of law provisions. The failure to enforce any right or provision herein shall not constitute a waiver of that right or provision. No waiver of any right or provision herein shall be effective unless made in writing and signed by the waiving party. Any waiver of a breach of a provision shall not constitute a waiver of any subsequent breach of that provision. If any provisions herein are found to be unenforceable on the grounds that they are overly broad or in conflict with applicable laws, it is the intent of the parties that such provisions be replaced, reformed or narrowed so that their original business purpose can be accomplished to the extent permitted by law, and that the remaining provisions shall not in any way be affected or impaired thereby.

suggestions.reason: The current survival clause exposes Quintiles, Inc. to two material enforcement gaps: it contains no express preservation of rights and liabilities that accrued before termination, meaning that claims Quintiles, Inc. has already earned or suffered — such as unpaid fees, completed indemnity triggers, or pre-termination breaches by Sponsor — could be argued to have lapsed upon termination. Additionally, the clause specifies no survival period, leaving the duration of Quintiles, Inc.'s protections (including indemnification and liability limitations that directly shield it from post-termination claims) legally uncertain and potentially subject to challenge. Both deficiencies together create a material risk that Quintiles, Inc.'s most valuable post-termination protections could be undermined in a dispute.
suggestions.original_text: Survival. The rights and obligations of Sponsor and Quintiles, which by intent or meaning have validity beyond such termination (including, but not limited to, rights with respect to inventions, confidentiality, publication, discoveries and improvements, indemnification and liability limitations) shall survive the termination of this Agreement or any Work Order.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Survival. All rights and obligations of Sponsor and Quintiles which by intent or meaning have validity beyond termination (including, but not limited to, rights with respect to inventions, confidentiality, publication, discoveries and improvements, indemnification and liability limitations), together with all rights and liabilities accrued by either party prior to termination, shall survive the termination of this Agreement or any Work Order indefinitely, or for such shorter period as may be expressly stated in the applicable provision.

suggestions.reason: The arbitration clause, as drafted, exposes Quintiles, Inc. to four material gaps: it fails to identify the governing law, leaving Quintiles without certainty as to which substantive rules apply in a dispute; it permits the counterparty to file for arbitration immediately without any prior negotiation period, depriving Quintiles of the opportunity to resolve disputes commercially before incurring arbitration costs; it contains no carve-out permitting Quintiles to seek urgent injunctive or equitable relief in court (critical where, for example, the counterparty misappropriates Quintiles' confidential information or intellectual property mid-dispute); and it imposes no obligation on the parties to continue performing during the pendency of a dispute, creating a risk that the counterparty could suspend its obligations and thereby disrupt Quintiles' project operations without consequence pending an award.
suggestions.original_text: Arbitration.
