Any controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement or the breach thereof shall be settled by arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association (“AAA”) under its Commercial Arbitration Rules, and judgment on the award rendered by the arbitrator shall be binding and may be entered in any court having jurisdiction thereof. Such arbitration shall be filed and conducted at the office of the AAA closest to the Quintiles office having responsibility for the Project, and shall be conducted in English by one arbitrator mutually acceptable to the parties selected in accordance with AAA Rules. The arbitrator shall not have the power to award any punitive damages or any damages excluded by this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The entire agreement clause broadly supersedes "all previous agreements (oral and written), negotiations and discussions" without expressly preserving either party's liability for fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation. Without a fraud carve-out, a counterparty could invoke this clause to defeat a claim by Quintiles, Inc. that it was induced to enter the Agreement or any Work Order on the basis of a fraudulent pre-contractual statement, arguing that all prior representations have been extinguished. This creates a material legal risk for Quintiles, Inc. in any dispute where the counterparty's pre-contractual conduct is at issue. The addition of a standard fraud carve-out is market practice in Master Services Agreements and does not alter the commercial balance of the provision.
suggestions.original_text: Entire Agreement, Headings and Modification. This Agreement, together with the applicable Work Orders, contains the entire understandings of the parties with respect to the subject matter herein, and supersedes all previous agreements (oral and written), negotiations and discussions. The descriptive headings of the sections of this Agreement are inserted for convenience only and shall not control or affect the meaning or construction of any provision hereof. suggestions.suggested_fix: Entire Agreement, Headings and Modification. This Agreement, together with the applicable Work Orders, contains the entire understandings of the parties with respect to the subject matter herein, and supersedes all previous agreements (oral and written), negotiations and discussions; provided, however, that nothing in this Agreement shall exclude or limit the liability of either party for fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation. suggestions.reason: The existing clause identifies only that the Master Agreement is incorporated by reference but establishes no hierarchy between the Master Agreement and this Work Order, no conflict-resolution mechanism, and no exclusion of extraneous terms such as Sponsor's purchase orders or standard terms. Without a clear order of priority, Sponsor could argue that a provision in this Work Order modifies or overrides a protection Quintiles, Inc. secured in the Master Agreement, exposing Quintiles, Inc. to unintended obligations or the loss of negotiated protections. The absence of an exclusion clause further creates a risk that Sponsor-issued purchase orders or online terms could be argued to form part of the contractual framework on a particular engagement.

Pursuant to the Master Agreement, Quintiles has agreed to perform certain services in accordance with written work orders, such as this one, entered into from time-to-time.

Pursuant to the Master Agreement, Quintiles has agreed to perform certain services in accordance with written work orders, such as this one, entered into from time-to-time.

suggestions.reason: The current clause identifies the Work Order and Master Agreement but contains no conflict-resolution mechanism, no express rule preventing this Work Order from overriding the Master Agreement, and no exclusion of extraneous terms. Without a priority rule, a counterparty could argue that Work Order terms—potentially more burdensome to Quintiles, Inc.—displace the protections negotiated in the Master Agreement, exposing Quintiles, Inc. to unintended financial and operational obligations. The absence of an exclusion of other terms also leaves open the risk that a counterparty's standard or online terms are incorporated by reference or course of dealing.
suggestions.original_text: Work Order. This document constitutes a “Work Order” under the Master Agreement and this Work Order and the services contemplated herein are subject to the terms and provisions of the Master Agreement.

suggestions.clause: Services and Payment of Fees and Expenses
suggestions.reason: The clause defers all fee and expense terms entirely to attachments without requiring those attachments to specify the basis on which fees are calculated or whether expenses are included in fees or billable above them. This leaves Quintiles, Inc. exposed to fee disputes and uncapped expense claims, since a counterparty could characterise costs as reimbursable extras without any contractual baseline requiring transparency on fee methodology or prior approval for additional charges. Without a minimum content standard on the face of the Work Order, Quintiles, Inc. has no enforceable protection if an attachment is silent, ambiguous, or subsequently challenged.
suggestions.original_text: Services and Payment of Fees and Expenses. The specific services contemplated by this Work Order (the “Services”) and the related payment terms and obligations are set forth on the following attachments, which are incorporated herein by reference:

suggestions.clause: Services and Payment of Fees and Expenses
suggestions.reason: The paragraph does nothing more than index the operative attachments and contains no standalone payment mechanics whatsoever—there is no invoicing timeline, no payment due date, no statement as to whether fees are fixed or variable, no invoice dispute procedure, and no late payment consequence. This exposes Quintiles, Inc. to significant financial and operational risk: without a payment due date or dispute mechanism, a counterparty could assert that undisputed invoices are payable immediately upon issuance, or conversely delay payment indefinitely, while Quintiles, Inc. has no express right to withhold contested amounts or recover interest on overdue sums. These omissions are material and should be addressed on the face of the Agreement rather than left entirely to Attachment 4, which is not before the reviewing party.
suggestions.original_text: SCOPE OF WORK – ATTACHMENT 1; PROJECT BUDGET – ATTACHMENT 2; TIMELINE – ATTACHMENT 3; PAYMENT SCHEDULE – ATTACHMENT 4; TRANSFER OF OBLIGATIONS (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 5; LOCAL REPRESENTATIVE DUTIES (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 6
suggestions.suggested_fix: SCOPE OF WORK – ATTACHMENT 1; PROJECT BUDGET – ATTACHMENT 2; TIMELINE – ATTACHMENT 3; PAYMENT SCHEDULE – ATTACHMENT 4; TRANSFER OF OBLIGATIONS (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 5; LOCAL REPRESENTATIVE DUTIES (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 6. Invoices shall be issued in accordance with the Payment Schedule set forth in Attachment 4. Payment of undisputed amounts is due within thirty (30) days of receipt of a valid invoice. Fees are fixed as set forth in Attachment 2 and may not be modified except by a written amendment executed by both parties. Quintiles, Inc. may dispute any invoice in writing within fifteen (15) days of receipt, stating the basis for the dispute in reasonable detail; disputed amounts shall be withheld pending good-faith resolution, and undisputed amounts shall remain due and payable when owed. Undisputed amounts not paid by the due date shall accrue interest at the lesser of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted exposes Quintiles, Inc. to significant operational and financial risk by deferring all termination mechanics to the Master Agreement without stating any grounds, notice requirements, written form requirements, cure periods, or consequences of termination within the Work Order itself. If the Master Agreement is silent or ambiguous on any of these elements, Quintiles, Inc. has no express contractual basis to terminate for material breach with a defined cure period, no right to payment for completed work upon early termination, and no clarity on when termination actually takes effect. The absence of a termination-for-convenience notice period further leaves Quintiles, Inc. exposed to abrupt termination without adequate protection for costs already incurred. The survival provision is only partially addressed and should be read alongside the Master Agreement's survival clause to confirm that payment obligations and confidentiality obligations survive Work Order termination.
suggestions.original_text: Term. The term of this Work Order shall commence on the date of execution and shall continue until the services described in Attachment 1 are completed, unless this Work Order is terminated in accordance with the Master Agreement. If the Master Agreement is terminated or expires, but this Work Order is not terminated or completed, then the terms of the Master Agreement shall continue to apply to this Work Order until the Work Order is either terminated or completed.

suggestions.reason: The clause fully binds affiliates to the Master Agreement and this Work Order, but imposes no equivalent obligations on non-affiliate subcontractors and consultants, leaving Quintiles, Inc. exposed to Sponsor claims arising from a subcontractor's breach of confidentiality, data protection, or security without a corresponding contractual chain of recourse against that subcontractor. Additionally, the listed subcontractors are fixed at execution with no mechanism governing Quintiles' ability to substitute or add subcontractors during performance, creating operational rigidity and potential Sponsor disputes if Quintiles must change its subcontracting arrangements mid-engagement. Both gaps create material financial and legal exposure for Quintiles, Inc. if a subcontractor incident occurs or if Sponsor contests an unilateral subcontractor change.
suggestions.original_text: Affiliates and Subcontractors. Sponsor agrees that Quintiles may use the services of its corporate affiliates to fulfill Quintiles’ obligations under this Work Order. Any such affiliates shall be bound by all the terms and conditions of, and be entitled to all rights and protections afforded under, the Master Agreement and this Work Order. Any subcontractors or consultants (other than Quintiles’ affiliates) that will be used by Quintiles in performing the Services are listed below:
suggestions.suggested_fix: Affiliates and Subcontractors. Sponsor agrees that Quintiles may use the services of its corporate affiliates to fulfill Quintiles' obligations under this Work Order. Any such affiliates shall be bound by all the terms and conditions of, and be entitled to all rights and protections afforded under, the Master Agreement and this Work Order. Any subcontractors or consultants (other than Quintiles' affiliates) that will be used by Quintiles in performing the Services are listed below, and Quintiles shall cause each such subcontractor and consultant to be bound by obligations at least equivalent to those imposed on Quintiles under the Master Agreement. Quintiles shall not engage any substitute or additional subcontractors or consultants without Sponsor's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, this clause is a bare placeholder that identifies approved subcontractors and consultants but contains no provision requiring the engaging party to remain responsible for their acts, omissions, or failures. For Quintiles, Inc., this creates a material gap: if the counterparty's subcontractor causes a breach, delivers non-conforming work, or gives rise to a third-party claim, the absence of a primary responsibility clause leaves Quintiles, Inc. without a clear contractual basis to hold the counterparty directly accountable. This exposure is compounded in an MSA context where subcontracting arrangements may change over the life of the Agreement without Quintiles, Inc. having visibility into or control over the subcontractor's performance.
suggestions.original_text: [Insert names of any subcontractors or consultants, other than Quintiles’ affiliates, that will be used]
suggestions.suggested_fix: [Insert names of any subcontractors or consultants, other than Quintiles' affiliates, that will be used]. The party engaging any such subcontractor or consultant shall remain primarily responsible for the performance of all obligations under this Agreement, and any act or omission of such subcontractor or consultant that would constitute a breach of this Agreement if performed by the engaging party shall be deemed a breach by that party.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the amendment clause is limited in scope to "this Work Order," leaving the Master Services Agreement itself and any other Schedules or attachments potentially modifiable without a written, signed amendment — a gap that exposes Quintiles, Inc. to arguments that informal communications or course-of-dealing altered its broader contractual rights. Additionally, the clause does not require execution by an authorized representative of each party, meaning a counterparty could contend that a signature by an employee without actual authority constitutes a binding amendment, undermining Quintiles, Inc.'s internal approval and governance controls. Both deficiencies are commercially material: the first narrows the written-amendment protection to a single Work Order rather than the full contractual framework, and the second removes a threshold safeguard against unauthorized modifications.
suggestions.original_text: Amendments. No modification, amendment, or waiver of this Work Order shall be effective unless in writing and duly executed and delivered by each party to the other.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Amendments. No modification, amendment, or waiver of this Agreement, including any Work Order or Schedule hereto, shall be effective unless in writing and duly executed and delivered by an authorized representative of each party to the other.

suggestions.reason: The Currency Exchange clause contains no operative language whatsoever — it is an unfilled drafting placeholder that imposes no rights, obligations, or protections on either party. For Quintiles, Inc., this creates direct financial exposure: where Quintiles earns fees or incurs expenses under a Work Order in a currency other than the invoice and payment currency, there is currently no mechanism to determine the applicable exchange rate, no allocation of currency fluctuation risk, and no basis on which Quintiles could recover losses arising from adverse exchange movements. A court could not give the provision any operative effect without recourse to extrinsic evidence, leaving Quintiles, Inc. financially unprotected on cross-currency Work Orders exceeding one million US Dollars.
suggestions.original_text: Currency Exchange. [Insert currency exchange provision in all Work Orders in which Quintiles will earn fees or incur expenses in excess of one million US. Dollars in a currency differing from the invoice and payment currency]
suggestions.suggested_fix: Currency Exchange. Where Quintiles incurs fees or expenses under a Work Order in a currency other than the invoice and payment currency in excess of one million US Dollars, the applicable exchange rate shall be the mid-market rate quoted by a recognized financial institution on the date such fee or expense is incurred, and all currency fluctuation risk shall be borne by Client.

suggestions.reason: The Inflation and Cost Adjustment clause consists entirely of an unfilled drafting placeholder and contains no operative language whatsoever, leaving Quintiles, Inc. with no contractual right to adjust fees for Services in response to rising costs, inflation, or increased overheads for the duration of the Agreement. Without a binding cost adjustment mechanism, Quintiles, Inc. is exposed to material financial erosion over multi-year engagements where labour, materials, and operating expenses increase but contractual rates remain fixed. The absence of any defined index, adjustment formula, timing, or notice mechanism means no court could enforce this provision as written, and any attempt by Quintiles, Inc. to unilaterally adjust fees would be contractually unsupported and subject to dispute.
